criteria: A function `slugify(title)` exists in `slugs.py` and turns a title into the last part of a link.
Rule 1: `slugify` lower-cases the title and keeps the letters `a`-`z` and the digits `0`-`9`: `slugify('Top 10')` returns `'top-10'`.

Rule 2: `slugify` turns every run of other characters into one hyphen, however long the run is, and an underscore is one of the other characters: `slugify('Hello,  World!')` returns `'hello-world'`, `slugify('a - b')` returns `'a-b'`, and `slugify('snake_case')` returns `'snake-case'`.
Rule 3: the result of `slugify` never starts or ends with a hyphen: `slugify('  --Rock & Roll--  ')` returns `'rock-roll'`.
Rule 4: `slugify` removes apostrophes, both `'` and `’`, before anything else, so they do not split a word: `slugify("Don't Stop")` returns `'dont-stop'`.

Rule 5: `slugify` keeps only the ASCII letters and digits of rule 1, and any other letter or digit, such as `é`, `ß` or `²`, counts as one of the other characters: `slugify('Café au lait')` returns `'caf-au-lait'` and `slugify('x² + 1')` returns `'x-1'`.
Rule 6: `slugify` returns the empty string for a title with nothing to keep, such as the empty string or `'!!!'`.
Rule 7: `slugify` raises `TypeError` when the title is not a `str`.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
